projectDescription: Native desktop widget that turns a claude.ai subscription's usage into pacing: burn-rate projection, pace markers, sparkline trends and themes. Two apps share the repo: a macOS SwiftUI app (Sparkle updates, Homebrew cask, GitHub Releases) with the Desk layer (desktop line, notch island, watchers, now playing), and a Windows .NET 10 / WPF app (Microsoft Store and Velopack). Both ship Claude Code integrations: a statusline, the network-free stdio MCP server, the sanduhr-meters mod, a usage vault, and Mods & Config with config packs and a marketplace publisher.
mainPurpose: Desktop application: an always-on-top glass widget that reads a claude.ai subscription's usage and local Claude Code token burn, and shows where you stand against pace before the reset
primaryUsers: Individual Claude Pro/Max/Team/Enterprise subscribers (solo devs, power users) who also run Claude Code. Public open source under MIT. Not an internal tool, not a customer-facing SaaS.
coreFeatures: Burn-rate projection ("At current pace, expires in 3d 21h") and an always-on pace ghost on every bar, with Cooldown required and Surplus on hover
Horizon sparkline over the last 2 hours and breathing glass
Five hand-tuned themes plus user-authored JSON themes, Theme Studio with lint, and themes proposed from Claude Code through propose_theme

Claude Code integrations: a statusline segment, the sanduhr stdio MCP server (get_usage, get_local_burn_by_project, get_model_usage, get_usage_history, ping, publish_usage, propose_theme, propose_mod, propose_config) and the sanduhr-meters mod, the meters band above the prompt; standard library only, reading snapshot.json and nothing that could hold a credential
The usage vault: a local per-account record of Claude Code sessions, read by day, week, project, model, tier and skill, with a CSV ledger

Mods & Config: a Catalog, By Seat and Compare for every Claude Code folder; Mod Studio; config packs (.sanduhrpack) to export, open and undo a folder's config, including an any-agent folder; Publish to Marketplace for kept mods
Desk (Mac): the desktop layer and notch island with the handwritten message line, meeting list, now playing, and camera and mic indicators
Watchers (Mac): live cards for work in flight, on a notch place or in a Desk corner
Multi-account support with per-account credentials and 30-day local history, stacked per-tier charts and CSV export
Deep-work focus timer with a digitised falling-sand hourglass, and the cooldown snake game
Sign in through claude.ai's own login in an in-app window; credentials in the macOS Keychain or Windows Credential Manager; no telemetry, one network destination
technologies: Sparkle (Mac auto-updates, appcast on GitHub Pages)
Python 3 standard library, 3.9+ (sanduhr_mcp.py MCP server, sanduhr_statusline.py, their tests)
.NET 10 / WPF with WebView2 (Windows app; Sanduhr.Core logic, Sanduhr.Mcp server, xUnit)
GitHub Actions (signed, notarized Mac releases; Windows CI and tag-triggered release)
Homebrew tap (cask) and DMG for macOS
Microsoft Store (MSIX) and Velopack (Setup.exe + delta feed) for Windows
Ruby smoke CLI for the running Mac app
Model Context Protocol (stdio) as the tool contract shared by both apps
deploymentModel: End-user desktop install, no server, no SaaS. macOS: Homebrew cask or a signed, notarized DMG from GitHub Releases, updated by Sparkle (24h check) or brew upgrade. Windows: Microsoft Store (signed MSIX, Store updates) or the Velopack installer from GitHub Releases, which updates itself from the release feed. Credentials stay in the OS credential store; the MCP server and statusline are installed from Settings into the user's Claude Code folders.
architectureStyle: Two native desktop apps sharing the docs, the release process and the MCP tool contract. Each is a frameless always-on-top widget that fetches usage from claude.ai with the user's own session cookie, keeps JSON history and a usage vault locally, and writes a snapshot file that the statusline, the MCP server and the meters mod read. Pure, tested core logic (Sanduhr.Core on Windows, Services and Helpers on the Mac) under a thin UI shell. No backend service: client-of-API, not a server.
